title: 2026 Title Defence: Destroyers Hold Nerve 3–2 to Complete Championship Three-Peat
summary: Destroyers defended their crown 3–2 in June 2026, sealing a third straight championship with a 12-run finale win at APSU Stadium.
body:

title: How Destroyers Trials Work: Earning the Derby Shirt
summary: From open trials to the 48-player pre-season camp — how Destroyers Cricket Club selects its squad for the derby season.
body:
Rewa, MP — Destroyers Cricket Club assembles an expanded pre-season training camp — most recently a 48-player group at APSU Stadium — ahead of each Atal Bihari Vajpayee Memorial Tournament cycle.

Trialists are assessed across formats with emphasis on derby temperament: strike rotation under pressure, death bowling execution and fielding intensity. Performance in local tournament cricket, alongside camp form, feeds final squad selection.

Trial windows and contact points are published through the club's contact desk before each season. Unsuccessful trialists are encouraged to reappear the following cycle.

title: Destroyers Announce 2025–26 Pre-Season Training Camp at APSU Stadium Led by Pranav Dwivedi
summary: Skipper Pranav Dwivedi leads a 48-man training squad ahead of the upcoming Atal Bihari Vajpayee Memorial Tournament season.
body:
Rewa, MP — Destroyers Cricket Club (DES) have formally launched their pre-season preparation for the 2025 and 2026 Atal Bihari Vajpayee Memorial Tournament cycles, assembling an expanded 48-player training camp at Awadhesh Pratap Singh University (APSU) Stadium.

Skipper and all-round talisman Pranav Dwivedi, who has amassed 1,341 runs and claimed 63 wickets across 24 fixtures against arch-rivals Dread Eleven (DE), emphasized the team’s momentum following their decisive 4–1 series win in 2024.

"Our rivalry with Dread Eleven has set the benchmark for competitive cricket in the Vindhya region," Dwivedi stated. "With Aryan Deshmukh, Shivam Shukla, Anubhav Agarwal, and Venkatesh Iyer providing depth across all departments, our focus is squarely on sustaining championship standards."

The 2025 campaign will kick off with an intense four-match series in September 2025, leading into the Silver Jubilee Tournament edition in 2026 under the auspices of the Rewa Division Cricket Association (RDCA).

title: RDCA Unveils Upgraded Turf Pitches at APSU Stadium for 2025–2026 Cycle
summary: The Rewa Division Cricket Association completes major renovations to pitch blocks and pavilion facilities ahead of upcoming fixtures.
body:
Rewa — The Rewa Division Cricket Association (RDCA) has officially concluded extensive rejuvenation work across the central pitch square at APSU Stadium, ensuring international-standard bounce and seam movement for the 2025 and 2026 seasons.

Chief Curator Rajesh Patel confirmed that local red soil combined with clay blends from the Narmada basin was utilized to reinforce the wickets against weathering while ensuring equitable contest between bat and ball.

"Both Destroyers and Dread Eleven showcase fast-paced, modern cricket. These revamped surfaces will reward authentic strokeplay while granting genuine pace bowlers true carry through to the wicketkeeper," Patel stated.

title: Dominant 2024 Campaign: How Destroyers Outplayed Dread Eleven 4–1 in 50-Over Series
summary: A tactical review of the 2024 50-over series where Destroyers captured four consecutive victories with clutch bowling and fearless batting.
body:
The 2024 season of the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Memorial Tournament marked a watershed moment for Destroyers Cricket Club, as they recorded a dominant 4–1 series conquest over Dread Eleven at APSU Stadium.

After dropping the opener by a solitary wicket, Destroyers rallied in spectacular fashion: winning by 5 runs on 8 September (257/6 vs 252/7), edging a thriller by 2 runs on 12 September (276 vs 274), cruising by 18 runs on 16 September (288/6 vs 270), and sealing the finale on 20 September with an 8-run triumph (233/6 vs 225).

Captain Pranav Dwivedi stood tall throughout the campaign, delivering key middle-overs breakthroughs and anchoring crucial partnerships alongside Aryan Deshmukh and Shivam Shukla.

title: All-Round Historic Milestone: Pranav Dwivedi Reaches 1,300 Runs & 60 Wickets in Derby Clashes
summary: Destroyers skipper becomes the first player in tournament history to achieve the elite double of 1,300+ runs and 60+ wickets.
body:
Destroyers captain Pranav Dwivedi has solidified his standing as the tournament’s most decorated competitor, surpassing 1,340 runs and 60 wickets across all 24 clashes against Dread Eleven.

Averaging 55.9 per innings with 13 half-centuries and a hundred to his name, Dwivedi has combined lethal top-order strokeplay with match-winning bowling spells (best bowling of 8/39). His endurance across all 24 encounters remains unmatched in Rewa division cricket history.

"Every run and every wicket is for Destroyers," Dwivedi remarked after concluding the 2024 season. "We have elevated this franchise to new heights, and our sights are firmly fixed on the 2025 and 2026 seasons."

summary: Banners, drums and full houses at APSU — inside the fan culture that turned Destroyers vs Dread Eleven into the Vindhya region's biggest rivalry.
body:
Rewa, MP — Ask anyone in Rewa what derby week means and the answer is the same: the town splits in two. Destroyers' red against Dread Eleven's colours, banners up at APSU Stadium and arguments in every tea shop.

The rivalry has produced everything from one-wicket finishes to a tied-run thriller and a 5–0 clean sweep, which is why travelling supporters plan derby week like a festival. Early arrival is advised — the popular stands fill well before the toss.

Win or lose, the derby handshake at full time has become its own tradition, and the return fixture is never more than a season away.

title: Know Your Derby Grounds: APSU Stadium and Martand No. 3 Venue Guide
summary: Where the Rewa derby lives — a supporter's guide to APSU Stadium and Martand School Ground No. 3, the two official derby venues.
body:
Rewa, MP — Every derby in the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Memorial Tournament is staged at one of two official grounds: the Awadhesh Pratap Singh University (APSU) Stadium and Martand School Ground No. 3, both in Rewa.

APSU Stadium hosts the marquee fixtures including the championship finals, while Martand No. 3 has staged several low-scoring thrillers decided in the final overs. Gates, parking and entry follow RDCA match-day advisories issued before each game.

Supporters travelling for derby week should check the fixtures page for venue confirmation, as late ground changes are announced via the official news feed.
